highlights.title: Agent tasks, full view
highlights.lead: Airc Agent tasks get their own view
highlights.detail: Open a task from the Agents folder to see every step, what it found and the agent's page live; reply or approve from there. ✦ or ⌥⌘A opens the compact pane.

highlights.title: Ask from ⌘T
highlights.lead: ⌘T can Ask as well as Search
highlights.detail: Press ⌘T, type what you want done and press Tab to ask the Airc Agent. Recent tasks show as cards under the field.

highlights.title: Spotify in Safari engine
highlights.lead: Spotify opens in Airc's Safari engine, where it plays
highlights.detail: Spotify now always opens in Airc's Safari engine, where its player works. Netflix and Disney+ still play in Chromium with the FairPlay setting, and Airc offers Safari's engine if a site can't play.

highlights.title: Faster first keystroke
highlights.lead: The Command Bar answers your first keystroke sooner
highlights.detail: Airc prepares the Command Bar while you're idle, so the first letter you type after ⌘T shows sooner.

highlights.title: A faster Chromium engine
highlights.lead: A faster Chromium engine
highlights.detail: Airc's Chromium engine is now built the way Chrome is, so windows are ready sooner after launch, busy pages use less CPU and Airc takes about 200 MB less space.

highlights.title: Typed sites not blocked
highlights.lead: Sites you type in are no longer blocked by mistake
highlights.detail: A site you type or open from a bookmark, such as analytics.google.com, no longer shows "blocked by Airc" in Chromium tabs. Trackers inside pages stay blocked.

highlights.title: Google tag tools work
highlights.lead: Google Tag Assistant and Tag Manager preview work with Airc's content blocking on
highlights.detail: On Google's Tag Assistant, Tag Manager and Analytics, Airc lets Google's tag scripts through so preview and debug mode connect. Everywhere else they stay blocked.

highlights.title: Your ChatGPT subscription
highlights.lead: Use your ChatGPT subscription in Airc Agent
highlights.detail: In Airc Agent (the ✦ button or ⌥⌘A), Connect your AI now starts with your ChatGPT subscription: connect your own Codex with Sign in with ChatGPT. Your own Claude Code or an API key work too.

highlights.title: Netflix and Disney+
highlights.lead: Netflix and Disney+ play in a Chromium tab with FairPlay
highlights.detail: Turn on Settings › Privacy › Protected content › Play protected media in Chromium with FairPlay (off by default): Netflix and Disney+ stay in a Chromium tab and play with Apple's FairPlay.

highlights.title: Airc Agent, one click away
highlights.lead: New ✦ button opens Airc Agent
highlights.detail: The new ✦ button at the bottom of the sidebar opens Airc Agent, or press ⌥⌘A. Right-click it for New Task, Watch or Settings › Agents.

highlights.title: Connect AI in the pane
highlights.lead: Connect your AI right in the pane, with no trip to Settings
highlights.detail: In Airc Agent (⌥⌘A), Connect your AI: your own Claude Code or Codex, or an API key. Keys stay in your Mac's Keychain.

highlights.title: Spotify plays in Chromium
highlights.lead: Play Spotify in a Chromium tab with FairPlay
highlights.detail: Turn on Settings › Privacy › Protected content › Play protected media in Chromium with FairPlay (off by default): Spotify stays in a Chromium tab with your extensions.

highlights.title: A short new-profile setup
highlights.lead: New profiles get a short setup: pick the Space's colour, sign in, done
highlights.detail: After Create Profile (a Space's Set Profile › New Profile…), pick a colour for the Space and sign in to Google in the new profile. The card then shows your account and closes.

highlights.title: Your account, right away
highlights.lead: Your account's picture and name show up right away, including after signing in from the sidebar
highlights.detail: After you sign in, including from the sidebar's Sign in to Google card, your account's picture and name show beside the Space name, in Set Profile › and in Settings › Profiles, without a relaunch.

highlights.title: Window buttons stay clear
highlights.lead: When Claude uses Airc, its notice no longer covers the window's close and minimize buttons
highlights.detail: While Claude or another AI app uses Airc, the sidebar shows "✦ Claude is using Airc" just under the window's buttons, never over them. Click it to Watch or Stop the app.

highlights.title: Saved logins stay safe
highlights.lead: Your saved passwords and cookies are safe if macOS can't unlock the keychain
highlights.detail: If macOS can't unlock the keychain, Airc asks you to Try Again instead of starting over. Your saved passwords and cookies stay, and they're back once the keychain opens.

highlights.title: Close any window
highlights.lead: Every window can be closed
highlights.detail: With the sidebar hidden, move the pointer to a window's top-left corner and its close button appears. ⌘W on a window's last tab closes the window, as in Arc.

highlights.title: A quicker Command Bar
highlights.lead: Typing in the Command Bar is quicker
highlights.detail: Each keystroke in the Command Bar (⌘T) does less work, and the first one after opening it no longer waits, so results keep up with your typing.

highlights.title: DevTools in the window
highlights.lead: Developer Tools dock inside the window you're inspecting
highlights.detail: Press ⌥⌘I and Developer Tools open beside the page in the same window, at the bottom or the side; ⇧⌘D switches. Every panel works, including the » list and right-click menus.

highlights.title: Set up Claude Code, Codex
highlights.lead: The agent pane can set up your own Claude Code or Codex
highlights.detail: In the agent pane (⌥⌘A), Install… shows the command to install your own Claude Code or Codex, and Sign in… starts its own sign-in. Hand back gives the agent the same tab.

highlights.title: A lighter agent pane
highlights.lead: The agent pane uses far less power while it's thinking
highlights.detail: While the Airc Agent is thinking, its pane now uses almost no CPU, so long tasks cost far less battery.

highlights.title: Stop shows in dark Spaces
highlights.lead: The Stop button in the agent pane shows in dark Spaces
highlights.detail: While the Airc Agent works, the round Stop button next to its message field is now visible in dark Spaces too.

highlights.title: The agent beside the page
highlights.lead: The Airc Agent opens beside the page
highlights.detail: Press ⌥⌘A and the Airc Agent opens next to your page. While it works, you see the page it's on, live, above the conversation.

highlights.title: Watch from the sidebar
highlights.lead: Watch any working agent from the sidebar
highlights.detail: Hover over a working task in the sidebar's Agents folder and click the eye to watch its page live.

highlights.title: Search in Settings
highlights.lead: Search in Settings
highlights.detail: Press ⌘F in Settings, or type in the field at the top of its sidebar. Pick a result to jump to that setting, highlighted.

highlights.title: Settings stays put
highlights.lead: Settings stays put
highlights.detail: Switching panes in Settings no longer moves the layout: every pane keeps the same column, and Appearance no longer shifts left.

highlights.title: Chromium security update
highlights.lead: Security update: Airc's Chromium engine is now 156.0.8078.109
highlights.detail: Airc's Chromium engine is now 156.0.8078.109, with Chrome's latest security fixes. Nothing to do: this update installs it.

highlights.title: Granola notes for calls
highlights.lead: Granola starts notes for your calls
highlights.detail: When a Meet, Zoom, Teams, Webex or Whereby tab turns on your microphone, Airc can start a Granola note, once per call. Turn it on in Settings › General › Calendar (shown when Granola is installed).

highlights.title: Password manager autofill
highlights.lead: Your password manager fills logins on its own
highlights.detail: Turn off Offer to save and fill passwords in Settings › Passwords, and Airc no longer fills a saved login when a page loads, so your password manager's extension does it instead.

highlights.title: Import from Dia
highlights.lead: Import from Dia
highlights.detail: Choose Dia in Airc › Import from Another Browser… to bring its profiles, bookmarks, history and extensions. With the Chromium engine, allow macOS to use Dia's key once and your passwords, cookies and sites' data come too.

highlights.title: Rules for connected apps
highlights.lead: Rules for each connected app
highlights.detail: In Settings › Agents › Apps, Rules… sets the one profile an app may use and sites it may never open. Agents upload only from folders you allow, and their downloads stay out of your list.

highlights.title: When a page needs you
highlights.lead: Agents tell you when a page needs you
highlights.detail: When an agent reaches a sign-in page or a captcha, its row in the Agents folder says Needs you and Airc sends a notification. Open it and Take over to sign in.

highlights.title: Dark mode for all of Airc
highlights.lead: Dark mode works
highlights.detail: In Settings › Appearance › Airc, choose Auto to follow your Mac, or Light or Dark for windows, the sidebar, Settings and every page. Spaces follow it unless you gave one its own look.

highlights.title: Better password managers
highlights.lead: Password-manager extensions work better
highlights.detail: 1Password's Unlock button now opens its popup, and Proton Pass, Bitwarden and 1Password popups open at full size. In Settings › Passwords you can let your password manager's extension save and fill logins instead of Airc.

highlights.title: Every app asked once
highlights.lead: Security: Airc now asks every app or script once before it can use the browser
highlights.detail: Airc now recognises apps and scripts by what actually runs, not the name they give, and asks each one once before it can use the browser. Some apps you allowed before are asked once more; see them in Settings › Agents.

highlights.title: Agent on your Claude Code
highlights.lead: Run the Airc Agent on your own Claude Code or Codex
highlights.detail: In Settings › AI › Agent › Use, choose Your Claude Code or Your Codex: the Airc Agent then runs your installed copy with its own login and only Airc's browser tools.

highlights.title: Tidier Agents folder
highlights.lead: The Agents folder tidies itself
highlights.detail: Rows in the sidebar's Agents folder now say what an agent did, like "Gmail · read 3 pages", and finished ones close after 5 minutes. Change that in Settings › Agents › Keep finished agents for.

highlights.title: Copy Quote Link
highlights.lead: Copy Quote Link, like Arc
highlights.detail: Select text on a page, then choose Copy Quote Link in its right-click menu or click Share Quote under the address. The link opens the page right at that text, highlighted.

highlights.title: Quiet notification sounds
highlights.lead: Notification sounds stay out of the sidebar player
highlights.detail: Short pings from pages such as WhatsApp or Slack no longer pop up the sidebar's mini player. Music and videos still get their player as before.

highlights.title: Command Bar fixes
highlights.lead: Command Bar fixes
highlights.detail: The Ask rows stay put while you type after ⌘T. "Ask This Page…" works on every page or says why, and "Ask Airc to…" shows even before you add an API key and opens the agent's setup.

highlights.title: Fast first launch: WebKit
highlights.lead: WebKit's first launch is fast too
highlights.detail: With the WebKit engine, a link opened on Airc's very first launch now shows in about a second instead of four: the blocking rules come ready to use.

highlights.title: Boosts sync
highlights.lead: Boosts sync between your Macs
highlights.detail: With iCloud sync on, your Boosts follow you to your other Macs. Their JavaScript runs only after a quick confirm on each Mac. Turn it off in Settings › Sync › Sync Boosts.

highlights.title: Quicker after updates
highlights.lead: The first launch after an update is a little quicker
highlights.detail: Airc now starts a downloaded update once in the background before it restarts, so macOS's first-run checks are already done. You'll notice it from the next update on.

highlights.title: Imported engines suggest
highlights.lead: Search suggestions from your imported search engines
highlights.detail: Search engines you brought over from Arc, Chrome or Brave now suggest as you type after ⌘T, like the built-in ones: your default, and a shortcut once you pick it with Tab. Not in private windows; turn suggestions off in Settings › Privacy.

highlights.title: Ask command from 2 letters
highlights.lead: "New ChatGPT Message" from the second letter
highlights.detail: The Command Bar now shows "New ChatGPT Message" (or "Ask Claude…") from the second letter you type, so your first keystroke after ⌘T stays fast.

highlights.title: Every launch is quick
highlights.lead: Every launch is quick now
highlights.detail: About every other launch used to wait up to a second inside macOS before Airc started, so a link from another app could take almost two seconds. That wait is gone with the Chromium engine, the default.

highlights.title: Links open fast
highlights.lead: Links open fast when Airc is closed
highlights.detail: Click a link in another app while Airc is closed and its page shows in about a second, even on the first launch (it used to take up to 6 seconds). Blocking still applies to the page from its first request.

highlights.title: Airc Agent (beta) improves
highlights.lead: Airc Agent (beta) gets better
highlights.detail: Replies stream in as they're written, and the approval card shows in Watch too. Turn on memory in Settings › AI › Agent, type a task in the Command Bar with "Ask Airc to…", or hand it to your Claude app.

highlights.title: Pages match light and dark
highlights.lead: Pages follow light and dark
highlights.detail: Web pages use their Space's light or dark look, and open pages switch at once when it changes, including when macOS switches between light and dark on its own. Background tabs, Peek and Little Airc follow too.

highlights.title: Airc Agent (beta)
highlights.lead: Airc Agent (beta)
highlights.detail: Press ⌥⌘A, describe a task, and Airc does it in your signed-in sites with your own Anthropic or OpenAI API key (add it in Settings › AI › Agent). It asks before it pays, sends, posts or deletes; Stop any time.

highlights.title: Settings sync between Macs
highlights.lead: Settings sync between your Macs
highlights.detail: With iCloud sync on, the settings you change (theme, shortcuts, Site Searches, blocking and more) follow you to your other Macs; the later change wins. Each Mac keeps its own folders, Developer Mode and app approvals. Settings › Sync › Sync settings.

highlights.title: Ask AI in the Command Bar
highlights.lead: Ask Claude or ChatGPT from the Command Bar
highlights.detail: Type a question or a prompt after ⌘T, press ↓↓ and Return: it opens in a new Claude or ChatGPT chat, signed in as you are. Pick the site, or Off, in Settings › AI › Command Bar › Ask AI.

highlights.title: Sign in to a new profile
highlights.lead: Signing in to a new profile from the sidebar
highlights.detail: When you sign in to Google from a new profile's sidebar card, the profile takes the account's picture and name, and the card offers Gmail, Calendar and Drive for that account as Favorites: Add or Skip.

highlights.title: Feedback, next to +
highlights.lead: The Feedback button sits next to +
highlights.detail: The speech bubble in the sidebar's bottom row now sits just left of +, after your Space icons. Click it to send a note or pictures to the Airc team.

highlights.title: Sign in with Google
highlights.lead: Sign in with Google works inside Airc
highlights.detail: On pages that use Chromium, "Continue with Google" shows Google's account chooser over the page again, so you pick an account right there instead of in a separate sign-in window.

highlights.title: Your calendar drives Join
highlights.lead: Your Google or Outlook calendar drives Join
highlights.detail: With Google Calendar or Outlook as a Favorite or pinned tab, Live Calendar's countdown, Join and ⌃⌘J use its events and call links (Meet, Zoom, Teams, Webex). Turn on Live Calendar in Settings › General.

highlights.title: Bangs in the Command Bar
highlights.lead: Bangs in the Command Bar
highlights.detail: Type a bang such as !yt cats, !gm Vienna or !gt hello in the Command Bar (⌘T) to search that site straight away. Your own Site Search shortcuts work as bangs too.

highlights.title: Steady search suggestions
highlights.lead: Search suggestions no longer flicker
highlights.detail: While you type in the Command Bar, the suggestions under it stay in place until new ones replace them, instead of blinking away with every letter.

highlights.title: Restart waits for pages
highlights.lead: Restart to Update waits for busy pages
highlights.detail: When you click Restart to Update, every page gets a few seconds to finish. If a tab has unsaved work, Airc shows you which one and asks: Restart Anyway or Cancel.

highlights.title: ⇧⌘R everywhere
highlights.lead: ⇧⌘R hard refresh
highlights.detail: ⇧⌘R reloads a page without its cached files. It now also works in Little Airc and in an open Peek, and reloads the page in front of you.

highlights.title: Lighter and quieter
highlights.lead: Lighter and quieter
highlights.detail: With WebKit, Airc's main process uses far less memory after launch. Switching Spaces is smoother, and an idle Airc no longer wakes up on repeating timers.

highlights.title: Airc from other devices
highlights.lead: Use Airc from your other devices
highlights.detail: Claude Code or another AI app on another computer on your Tailscale network can use Airc on this Mac. Turn it on and pair each device with a one-time code in Settings › Agents › Other devices; Revoke ends a device's access.

highlights.title: Google sign-in crash fixed
highlights.lead: Fixed a crash when signing in with Google on some sites (e.g. Pinterest)
highlights.detail: With the Chromium engine, "Continue with Google" on sites such as Pinterest could quit Airc. Sign-in now opens Google's own sign-in window instead.

highlights.title: Six-hour calendar cards
highlights.lead: Calendar previews fit Arc's six hours
highlights.detail: Rest the pointer on a pinned Google Calendar or Outlook tab to see six hours without scrolling. A Google or Outlook calendar Favorite now shows that calendar's own day, not your Mac's calendars.

highlights.title: Lighter Command Bar typing
highlights.lead: Typing in the Command Bar is lighter again
highlights.detail: Each letter you type in the Command Bar takes less work, with the same results. Services from other apps, like "Ask Claude", no longer show up there as commands that do nothing.

highlights.title: AI apps see page headings
highlights.lead: AI apps see page headings
highlights.detail: When Claude or another AI app reads a page in Airc, it gets the page's headings with their levels, so it finds its way around long pages. Hidden headings are left out.

highlights.title: Steadier update downloads
highlights.lead: Update downloads come straight from aircbrowser.com
highlights.detail: Airc's updates now download through aircbrowser.com itself instead of a separate storage host, so they no longer stall on some networks.

highlights.title: Connect Claude in one step
highlights.lead: Connect Claude in one step
highlights.detail: Type "claude" in the Command Bar, or choose Help › Use Airc with Claude…, and Settings › Agents opens with Add to Claude Desktop first. Access then says whether an app has connected.

highlights.title: Calendar hour grid
highlights.lead: Calendar previews show Arc's hour grid again
highlights.detail: Rest the pointer on a pinned Google Calendar or Outlook tab to see the next hours as a grid, with overlapping meetings side by side, a line at the current time and tomorrow's events below.

highlights.title: Updates retry on their own
highlights.lead: Updates retry by themselves
highlights.detail: If an update download stalls, Airc gives up after 20 seconds and quietly tries once more, so updates arrive without you doing anything.

highlights.title: Export All Easels
highlights.lead: Export All Easels
highlights.detail: The card at the top of Library › Easels saves every Easel as a web page in one ZIP, while you keep working. File › Export Easel… now lets you pick Image or Web Page.

highlights.title: Dark icons stay visible
highlights.lead: Dark site icons stay visible
highlights.detail: In a dark theme, a site icon that is itself dark, such as a black letter, now sits on a small light plate so it doesn't disappear into the sidebar.

highlights.title: More Show me buttons
highlights.lead: What's New's Show me goes further
highlights.detail: Show me on this page can now also open Settings › AI and Settings › Shortcuts, and each update can explain up to seven new things.

highlights.title: Watch your AI agents
highlights.lead: See what your AI agent is doing
highlights.detail: When Claude or another AI app uses Airc, its tabs appear in an Agents folder in the sidebar. Click one to watch it live, then take it over as your own tab or stop it. Settings › Agents › Activity lists what agents did.

highlights.title: What's New in Airc
highlights.lead: What's New in Airc
highlights.detail: After an update, Airc opens this tab to explain each new thing, with a button that takes you to it. Choose a tab, a card in the sidebar, or nothing in Settings › General.

highlights.title: Dark mode reads better
highlights.lead: Dark mode reads better
highlights.detail: Text in dark mode now meets standard contrast in every Space colour, so labels, addresses and the Command Bar's rows are easier to read. Dark Spaces are a little deeper.

highlights.title: Automatic download names
highlights.lead: Tidy Downloads renames automatically
highlights.detail: Turn on Rename automatically in Settings › AI › Downloads, and a download with an unclear name gets a clear one by itself, with Undo right after. It needs Apple Intelligence.

highlights.title: Share Quote
highlights.lead: Share Quote
highlights.detail: Select a few words on a page and a Share Quote button shows under the address. Click it to copy a link that opens the page at that text. You can turn it off in Settings › General.

highlights.title: Command Bar opens at once
highlights.lead: The Command Bar opens instantly
highlights.detail: The Command Bar is the box where you type a site, a search, an open tab or a command. Press ⌘T anywhere and it now appears in the very next frame, so the first letters you type always land in it.

highlights.title: Pick Airc's app icon
highlights.lead: More app icons
highlights.detail: Choose the icon Airc shows in the Dock, the app switcher and the Finder: six of Airc's own, from Holographic to Sunset, Ocean, Midnight and Graphite. Your choice stays after updates.

highlights.title: Splits sync between Macs
highlights.lead: Splits sync between your Macs
highlights.detail: A split shows two or more pages side by side in one tab. With iCloud Sync on, the splits you pinned or made Favorites now appear on your other Macs too, in the same order and sizes.

highlights.title: Calendar previews
highlights.lead: Calendar previews
highlights.detail: Rest the pointer on a pinned Google Calendar or Outlook calendar tab to see today's and tomorrow's events without switching to it. Click an event to open it there.

highlights.title: Opens faster
highlights.lead: Opens faster
highlights.detail: Airc's window now appears right away when you open it, instead of waiting for the ad and tracker blocker. Pages still wait for it, so nothing loads unprotected.

highlights.title: Complete Arc import
highlights.lead: Arc import, complete
highlights.detail: Importing from Arc now also brings your saved logins, cookies and sites' stored data, so you stay signed in to your sites. It needs the Chromium engine.

highlights.title: Notes and Easels in Peek
highlights.lead: Notes and Easels open in Peek
highlights.detail: Click a note or an Easel in the Library and it opens in Peek, a window floating over your page, ready to edit. Open in Space puts it back in the sidebar.

highlights.title: Clear Archive by age
highlights.lead: Clear Archive by age
highlights.detail: The Archive keeps the tabs Airc tidied away for you. You can now clear all of it, or only tabs older than 7 or 30 days, with Undo right after.

highlights.title: See a Boost's code first
highlights.lead: See a Boost's code first
highlights.detail: A Boost restyles or changes a website for you. When you add one someone shared, Airc shows its full code before anything runs, and a Boost with code starts switched off.

highlights.title: Claude can use Airc
highlights.lead: Let Claude use your browser
highlights.detail: AI apps such as Claude Desktop and Claude Code can open pages, read them, click and type for you, in windows of their own. Airc asks once per app and never shows one your passwords.

highlights.title: What's new, in Airc
highlights.lead: What's new, in Airc itself
highlights.detail: After an update Airc tells you what changed, on a page like this one or as a small card in the sidebar. Choose which, or neither, in Settings › General.

highlights.title: Feedback with pictures
highlights.lead: A Feedback button in the sidebar
highlights.detail: The speech bubble at the bottom of the sidebar sends a note to the Airc team. Add up to five pictures by pasting, dropping, or capturing the window.

highlights.title: Copy link from the sidebar
highlights.lead: Copy a link from the sidebar
highlights.detail: Every tab in the sidebar has a copy button next to its ×. Click it to copy the tab's link without switching to it.

highlights.title: Full-screen new windows
highlights.lead: New windows in full screen
highlights.detail: When Airc is in full screen, ⌘N opens the new window in a full-screen Space of its own, instead of floating over the one you're in.

highlights.title: Right-click menus
highlights.lead: Right-click menus on web pages

highlights.title: Open Link in Space
highlights.lead: Open Link in Space, in every link menu

highlights.title: Full extension list
highlights.lead: Every extension to reinstall, when you import from Arc

highlights.title: Spaces saved on quit
highlights.lead: Your Spaces are saved as soon as you quit

highlights.title: No more held tabs
highlights.lead: No more "held" tabs

highlights.title: Favorite badges, as in Arc
highlights.lead: Favorite badges, as in Arc

highlights.title: Search engines imported
highlights.lead: Your search engines come along

highlights.title: Add shared Easels
highlights.lead: Add to Airc for shared Easels

highlights.title: Send Feedback
highlights.lead: Send Feedback

highlights.title: Previews show their age
highlights.lead: Tab previews show their age

highlights.title: Turn off one tab's preview
highlights.lead: Turn off one tab's preview

highlights.title: VoiceOver reads previews
highlights.lead: VoiceOver reads tab previews

highlights.title: Preview cards stay put
highlights.lead: Preview cards stay put
